learningObjective: Compute liveness at a program point given standard live-in / live-out equations.

canonicalClaims.claim: For instruction I with use[I] and def[I]: live_in[I] = (live_out[I] − def[I]) ∪ use[I]. Liveness is a backward may-analysis; at a block boundary, live_out[B] = ∪ live_in[succ].
conditions: SSA or non-SSA IR with well-defined use/def sets per instruction.
No aliasing between named variables (each name is a distinct value).
nonImplications: Does not imply liveness alone determines register allocation; interference graphs and coloring add further constraints.
Does not imply must-live and may-live variants agree; the standard formulation is may-live.

misconceptions.claim: Liveness is a forward analysis computing which variables have been defined.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Liveness is backward; it computes which variables will be used before being redefined along some future path.

misconceptions.claim: Defined variables are always included in live-in of their defining instruction.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Definitions kill live-in; a variable is only live-in if it is used before being (re)defined.

misconceptions.claim: Liveness only propagates through the same block.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Liveness is a global analysis; live_out[B] aggregates live_in of successor blocks.

implementationFacts: Initial live-out at exit block: empty.
Iterate to fixpoint over the CFG (typically in reverse post-order for efficient convergence).
performanceScenarios: Register allocators use liveness to build interference graphs; more precise liveness (SSA-based) yields tighter graphs.
